exam: 1984 AP Chemistry MCQ · Version indicated in source
text:
84.  Which of the following aqueous solutions has the
     highest boiling point?

    A)  0.10 M potassium sulfate, K2SO4
    B)  0.10 M hydrochloric acid, HCl
    C)  0.10 M ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3
    D)  0.10 M magnesium sulfate, MgSO4
    E)  0.20 M sucrose, C12H22O11

candidates.name: Colligative properties and molality
candidates.definition: Freezing-point depression, boiling-point elevation, osmotic pressure and vapor-pressure lowering, and molality. Removed from the current AP Chemistry exam.
candidates.include: Tag legacy questions that require these calculations or explanations.
candidates.exclude: Never present as current AP exam content.

candidates.name: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
candidates.definition: Using the relative strength of intermolecular forces to explain or rank boiling point, melting point, vapor pressure, viscosity, surface tension or enthalpy of vaporization, and distinguishing intermolecular from intramolecular forces.
candidates.include: Tag when a physical property must be compared or explained in terms of intermolecular attractions; pair with the specific force concept(s) that decide the comparison.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag chemical reactivity or bond-breaking explanations; boiling does not break covalent bonds.
